name: Frankenstein
hook: A teenage ghost story that became the monster Jeopardy asks about most.

facts.label: Mary Shelley
facts.statement: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein at 18, inspired by Galvani's electrical experiments, and published it anonymously in 1818; she dedicated it to her father, William Godwin.

facts.label: Mary Wollstonecraft
facts.statement: Mary Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman in 1792 and died after giving birth to Mary Shelley.
associations: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

facts.label: The Modern Prometheus
facts.statement: Its subtitle is 'The Modern Prometheus'; Percy Shelley, author of Prometheus Unbound, urged Mary to write it and supplied the preface.

facts.label: Victor Frankenstein
facts.statement: Victor Frankenstein is the scientist who creates the creature; his name is routinely confused with the monster's.

facts.label: Boris Karloff
facts.statement: Boris Karloff played the creature in the 1931 film, with Colin Clive as Dr. Frankenstein.

facts.label: Bride of Frankenstein
facts.statement: The 1935 sequel starred Elsa Lanchester, who was married to Charles Laughton.

facts.label: Young Frankenstein
facts.statement: Mel Brooks's 1974 comedy starred Gene Wilder as Dr. Frankenstein and Marty Feldman as the hunchback assistant Igor.
